Reading

The innocent reading first, in full: asked for the journal by name, the Overview gives what a reader would want first: what the journal is, when it was founded, who publishes and edits it, how often it appears, its identifiers, its scope, and where to find its current and back issues, and offers to help with submission or with past articles. It is accurate on every fact it states.

Findings
  • THE SELF-DESCRIPTION AS STATEMENT. The Overview's first sentence is the journal's own description, carried without attribution: 'an internationally respected, peer-reviewed academic journal dedicated to the study of the life, languages, and thought of the ancient Greek and Roman world'. Its source is the journal's page at the department ('Classical Philology (CP) has been an internationally respected journal … since 1906'), which Duotrope's listing reproduces under its own 'About' heading; the Overview adds Wikipedia's 'peer-reviewed academic', writes 'dedicated to' for 'for', and moves 'since 1906' into its masthead list. (Corrected 2026-11-17 on the /non row's field ledger: the earlier wording gave the words as the journal's 'About'.)
  • THE MASTHEAD AS CONTENT. Founded 1906; The University of Chicago Press; Editor-in-Chief Sarah Nooter; 4 issues a year; ISSN 0009-837X / 1546-072X. Scope as a list of fields. No article, no finding, no decision of the journal is named.
  • THE RECORD ROUTED TO THE GATE. 'Current Content: Available via the Classical Philology Current Issue page'; 'Back issues and historical volumes can be explored through JSTOR'. The closing offer is submission or 'specific past articles'.
  • THE PANEL. The Press's About page shows '2025 CiteScore*: 1.0. Ranked #15 out of 196 “Classics” journals'; the composition does not carry it. A card for the American Journal of Philology (Hopkins Press, editor Rosa Andújar) sits among the journal's own.
  • THE WIKIPEDIA STUB (notes). Three sentences and an infobox, marked a stub, last edited three months before the reading. The operator's view showed related articles for Paul Shorey, Charles H. Beeson and Gertrude Smith (the live page carries no such block; it is a feature of the reader's view); that the three were editors rests on the masthead (Dead Letters §8.6.1: Shorey the founding editor; Beeson and Gertrude Smith on the 1923 and 1930 boards), not on the page. The operator: 'aio has almost nothing to say. and jesus - thats the scantest wikipedia article ive ever seen'. (Corrected 2026-11-17 on the /non row's field ledger.)
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

What the composition holds about the journal is its self-description and its masthead. Its first sentence is the journal's own description, 'an internationally respected, peer-reviewed academic journal dedicated to the study of the life, languages, and thought of the ancient Greek and Roman world', the words Duotrope's listing carries ('has been an internationally respected journal for the study of the life, languages, and thought…'), stated as the Overview's own. The facts are the masthead's: 1906, the Press, the editor, four issues, two ISSNs. The scope is a list of fields. Nothing in it says what the journal has published, decided or argued, or how it decides; the only access route given for the record is the current issue and JSTOR. The panel carries a ranking ('2025 CiteScore*: 1.0. Ranked #15 out of 196 “Classics” journals') that the composition does not use, and a card for a different journal (the American Journal of Philology). The Wikipedia article the operator opened from the panel is a stub of three sentences whose related articles are three past editors. Read with the census (Dead Letters §8, §8.7): the publisher's metadata deposit carries no abstract, and the public account of the institution is its self-description and its masthead.
